question: What is the recommended minimum birth spacing interval to protect maternal and child health?
explanation: Waiting two to three years between pregnancies allows the mother's body to recover fully and reduces risks for the newborn. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T1#GNS225_U3_T1_h1)

question: How does proper birth spacing directly help keep mothers safe?

options.A: By reducing complications like severe bleeding and exhausted uterine muscles
options.B: By ensuring all deliveries happen exclusively at home
options.C: By guaranteeing that mothers will never experience morning sickness
options.D: By completely eliminating the need for antenatal care visits

explanation: You've got this! Proper spacing gives the uterus time to rest between pregnancies, which greatly lowers the risk of heavy bleeding (hemorrhage). Great nursing insight to keep in mind! [learn more](GNS225_U3_T1#GNS225_U3_T1_h1)

question: What is a major advantage that barrier methods like condoms have over hormonal methods?

options.A: They never need to be replaced or bought again
options.C: They require no active participation during intercourse
options.D: They completely stop menstrual bleeding forever

explanation: Spot on! While hormonal methods prevent pregnancy, only barrier methods like condoms give that dual protection against STIs as well. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T1#GNS225_U3_T1_h2)

question: During natural family planning, what does a woman look for when checking her cervical mucus for peak fertility?

options.A: A thick, sticky discharge that remains present all month
options.B: A brownish bloody discharge right before ovulation
options.C: Complete dryness with no vaginal secretions at all
options.D: Clear, stretchy mucus that looks like raw egg white

explanation: Think of raw egg whites! When ovulation approaches, the mucus changes texture to help sperm swim easily toward the egg. Simple and natural! [learn more](GNS225_U3_T1#GNS225_U3_T1_h2)

question: Which contraceptive option is a long-acting reversible method placed right inside the uterus?
explanation: An IUD is a fantastic, worry-free option that sits quietly inside the uterus for years, providing continuous protection that you can stop anytime. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T1#GNS225_U3_T1_h3)

question: How do standard daily contraceptive pills primarily prevent pregnancy?

options.A: By permanently blocking the fallopian tubes with scar tissue
options.B: By stopping ovulation and changing the cervical mucus
options.C: By killing all bacteria inside the vaginal canal
options.D: By neutralizing stomach acid so hormones cannot absorb

explanation: The hormones in the pill do a double-duty job: they tell the body to pause ovulation and make the cervical mucus thick so sperm can't get through. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T1#GNS225_U3_T1_h3)

question: What is the primary male surgical sterilization procedure called?
explanation: A vasectomy blocks or cuts the vas deferens tubes to prevent sperm from entering the semen. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T1#GNS225_U3_T1_h4)

question: A client considering a tubal ligation is worried it will ruin her sex life and stop her periods. What should you tell her?

options.A: Explain that the surgery only blocks the tubes and does not affect hormones, sexual desire, or menstrual cycles
options.B: Agree that she will enter early menopause and lose all sexual interest immediately
options.C: Tell her that her periods will stop completely because her ovaries will be removed
options.D: Suggest she use emergency contraceptive pills instead of surgery forever

explanation: As a nurse, part of your job is reassurance! Tubal ligation only blocks the path for the egg and sperm; her ovaries stay safe and keep producing her normal hormones. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T1#GNS225_U3_T1_h4)

question: Why is it so important to use a client-centered approach during family planning counseling?

options.A: It allows the nurse to choose the most expensive method available
options.B: It stops the client from asking questions about side effects
options.C: It guarantees that the client will choose permanent sterilization
options.D: It ensures the client selects a method that fits her lifestyle and health needs

explanation: Nursing is all about the patient! When a client helps choose her own method, she feels respected and is much more likely to use it correctly. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T1#GNS225_U3_T1_h5)

question: Which quick physical check is critical before prescribing a combined estrogen-progestin oral contraceptive?
explanation: Always check the BP first! Estrogen can sometimes cause blood pressure to rise or increase clot risks, so checking baseline BP keeps your client safe. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T1#GNS225_U3_T1_h5)

question: What is a common local myth in Nigeria regarding modern contraceptives and young women?

options.A: That using them before having children causes permanent infertility
options.B: That they cause women to grow facial hair overnight
options.C: That they are only manufactured for elderly grandmothers
options.D: That they instantly cure all infectious diseases

explanation: This is a very common community worry. As future nurses, you'll help clear up this misconception by explaining that modern methods do not cause permanent damage. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T1#GNS225_U3_T1_h6)

question: A community nurse meets resistance from male elders who think family planning promotes promiscuity. What is the best first step?

options.A: Ignore the elders completely and hand out contraceptives secretly behind their backs
options.B: Engage the men in respectful dialogue, emphasizing child spacing, maternal health, and family financial stability
options.C: Argue with them aggressively to prove that their traditional beliefs are entirely wrong
options.D: Report the entire village community to the local police station immediately

explanation: Community health nursing requires patience and respect. Sitting down to talk with community leaders helps frame family planning around health, peace, and family well-being. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T1#GNS225_U3_T1_h6)
